title: Carbon and Low-Alloy Steel Classifications
description: Steel classification tool that covers carbon steel and low-alloy steel compositions, manufacturing methods, finishing techniques, product forms, deoxidation practices, microstructure types, strength levels, heat treatments, and quality descriptors according to ASTM standards.

components.content:
## Steel Classification Overview

Steel is considered to be carbon steel when no minimum content is specified or required for chromium, cobalt, columbium (niobium), molybdenum, nickel, titanium, tungsten, vanadium or zirconium.

### Classification Factors

- **Composition**: Carbon, low-alloy or stainless steel
- **Manufacturing Methods**: Open hearth, basic oxygen process, or electric furnace methods
- **Finishing Method**: Hot rolling or cold rolling
- **Product Form**: Bar, plate, sheet, strip, tubing or structural shape
- **Deoxidation Practice**: Killed, semi-killed, capped or rimmed steel
- **Microstructure**: Ferritic, pearlitic and martensitic
- **Strength Level**: As specified in ASTM standards
- **Heat Treatment**: Annealing, quenching and tempering, and thermomechanical processing
- **Quality Descriptors**: Forging quality and commercial quality

For more information, visit [Key to Metals - Steel Classifications](http://www.keytometals.com/page.aspx?ID=CheckArticle&LN=EN&site=KTS&NM=62)
